title: Negotiation basics
examples: What is the difference between an interest and a position?
Can you give me an example of a good BATNA?
How do I make a negotiation a win-win situation?

explain.say: Today we are learning about negotiation basics skills. You will learn to find common ground with others. This helps you reach better agreements together.

items: Negotiation is talking to reach an agreement.
It requires understanding other people's needs.

explain.say: First we must learn to separate interests from positions. A position is what you say you want. Your interest is the underlying need you have.
Next we look at your BATNA, which stands for Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement. This is your plan if talks fail.

draw.text: BATNA: Best Alternative To Negotiated Agreement

explain.say: Remember that a strong BATNA gives you power at the table. It means you are prepared to walk away if things go wrong.
Finally we aim for a win-win outcome in any negotiation. This means both sides feel they gained something valuable. It is a mutually beneficial result.

Consider planning a group project with a friend. Your position might be doing all the research. Your interest is getting a good grade. A good BATNA is finding another group. A win-win is splitting the work fairly.

faq.q: What is the difference between an interest and a position?
faq.a: A position is a specific demand, like needing a raise. Your interest is the reason you need that raise, such as feeling valued at work. You might also ask, 'What is the difference between a want and a need?' or 'Can you give me an example of an interest?'
asks: How do I find my true interest?

faq.q: Why is having a strong BATNA so important?
faq.a: A strong BATNA gives you confidence because you know you have a good fallback plan. If the negotiation fails, you are not left with no options. You could also ask, 'What if my BATNA is bad?' or 'Does my BATNA have to be perfect?'
asks: How strong does my alternative need to be?

faq.q: How do I make sure the outcome is truly win-win?
faq.a: A win-win means both parties walk away feeling satisfied with the outcome. It requires actively listening to understand the other person's true needs. You could also ask, 'What if one side really wants it more?' or 'Is win-win always possible?'
asks: How do I make sure both people are happy?
What if the other person is difficult?

faq.q: Can I use my BATNA to pressure the other person?
faq.a: You can use it as leverage, but using it aggressively can damage the relationship. The goal is to present it calmly as a solid alternative. You might ask, 'Is it okay to mention my BATNA?' or 'When should I bring up my alternative?'
asks: Is it okay to threaten to leave?
How do I use my alternative without sounding aggressive?

faq.q: If I only focus on my interests, will I be selfish?
faq.a: Focusing on your interests is about self-advocacy, not selfishness. You must still acknowledge and validate the other person's interests. You could also ask, 'Do I have to compromise everything?' or 'How much should I care about them?'
asks: Should I only think about myself?
What is the balance between my needs and theirs?

facts: A position is a stated demand, while an interest is the underlying need.
BATNA stands for Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement.
A win-win outcome means all parties benefit from the agreement.
Knowing your BATNA strengthens your negotiating power.

quiz.say: My position is that I must have a new phone. My underlying interest is to stay connected with my family. What is the interest?

options.show: To stay connected with my family.
options.say: To stay connected with my family.

options.show: I must have a new phone.
options.say: I must have a new phone.

quiz.why: The interest is the 'why' behind the position, which is the need for connection.

wrong.0: This is a specific desire, which is closer to a position than a core need.
wrong.2: This is the position, not the underlying need.
wrong.3: This is a possible interest, but 'staying connected' is more specific to the prompt.

quiz.say: If I cannot agree on a project deadline, my best alternative is to ask a teacher for an extension. What is this alternative called?
quiz.why: Your best alternative plan if the negotiation fails is your BATNA.

wrong.0: A position is what you demand, not what you do next.
wrong.1: An interest is the need, not the concrete alternative action.
wrong.3: Win-Win describes a successful outcome, not the fallback plan.

quiz.say: If I get a new job, and both my boss and I feel happy with the salary and the flexible hours, what outcome did we achieve?
quiz.why: When both people benefit equally, the outcome is called win-win.

wrong.0: Position only describes what one side demanded.
wrong.1: BATNA is the plan for when things go wrong, not the successful result.
wrong.2: Interest is the underlying need, not the final agreement.
